reasons.D: Closest movement and stance: short declaratives cut against longer ones, dry irony ('It was very good advice, and he did not take it'), a first-person turn and a wry, aphoristic close match the author's genial, ironic essayist voice.
reasons.B: Good rhythm, with rhetorical questions and a clipped aphoristic ending that echo the author, but the tone is a touch more earnest and argumentative and has less of his playful irony.
reasons.A: Right period diction and some short, pointed sentences, but the stance is steadier and more solemn, the clauses are more even, and it lacks the author's quick turns and exclamatory or questioning energy.
reasons.C: Modern, explanatory register ('the hard way', 'the lesson for our own time is uncomfortable'), with smooth, uniform sentences and none of the author's irony, questions or homely figures.
